user.title: Connect to your LLM provider
user.description:
Point this at any OpenAI-compatible server, such as vLLM, SGLang, LiteLLM or fastllm proxy. The URL may be the host on its own; /v1 is added if missing.

You add models to this provider in the next step.

data_description.api_key: Leave empty if the endpoint needs no authentication.

reconfigure.title: Provider settings
reconfigure.description: Change the endpoint or the API key. Models configured on this provider are kept.

data_description.api_key: Leave empty if the endpoint needs no authentication.

reauth_confirm.title: Provider key rejected
reauth_confirm.description: {base_url} rejected the stored API key. Enter a current one.

data_description.api_key: Leave empty if the endpoint no longer needs authentication.

error.cannot_connect: Could not reach that endpoint. Check the URL and that the server is running.
error.invalid_auth: The endpoint rejected that API key.

abort.already_configured: That endpoint is already set up. Add a model to it instead.

user.title: Choose a model
user.description: Pick a model from the provider. It is then tested to see what it supports.

data_description.name: Shown in Home Assistant, for example Voice or Study.
data_description.model: Chosen from what the provider serves. Type a name if it is not listed.

data_description.llm_hass_api: Which tool APIs the model may use. Without one it can talk but not act.
data_description.assistant_name: What the agent calls itself. Match your wake word so it stays consistent.

data_description.prompt: The agent's persona. {name} is replaced with the assistant name above.
data_description.vision: Set from testing the model. Servers accept images for text-only models and quietly ignore them, so this is measured by whether an image costs prompt tokens. Turn it off if you would rather not send camera snapshots.
data_description.thinking: Reasoning models answer better but take seconds longer and spend much of the token budget before replying. Off unless you need it.
data_description.max_tokens: How long a reply may be. Reasoning models spend much of this before answering, so do not set it low.
data_description.timeout: How long to wait between streamed tokens before giving up.
data_description.tool_mode: Native uses the endpoint's tool calling and is right for vLLM, SGLang and LiteLLM. Prompted describes the tools in the prompt and reads the reply for a call, for small models whose stack offers none - it is less reliable and the reply cannot start being spoken until it is complete. None lets the agent talk without acting.
data_description.language: Leave empty to answer in whatever language you are addressed in. Set a language and the agent always replies in it. Note that your voice assistant's text-to-speech voice has its own language: if they disagree you get correct text read in the wrong accent.
data_description.temperature: Left at the default it is not sent at all and the server's own default applies. Some providers refuse a request that sets both temperature and top P.
